title: Sort Linked List Already Sorted Using Absolute Values
summary: Given a singly linked list sorted by the absolute values of its nodes, return the list sorted by the actual values of its nodes in non-decreasing order.
statement: Given a singly linked list sorted by the absolute values of its nodes, return the list sorted by the actual values of its nodes in non-decreasing order.
constraints: The singly linked list is sorted by nondecreasing absolute node value.
Rearrange existing nodes into nondecreasing actual value order.
Return the new head; an empty list remains empty.
reference_solution:
def sort_absolute_sorted_list(head):
    negative=None;nonnegative_dummy=ListNode(0);nonnegative=nonnegative_dummy
    node=head
    while node:
        following=node.next
        if node.val<0:node.next=negative;negative=node
        else:nonnegative.next=node;nonnegative=node;node.next=None
        node=following
    if negative is None:return nonnegative_dummy.next
    tail=negative
    while tail.next:tail=tail.next
    tail.next=nonnegative_dummy.next
    return negative

hints: Absolute sorting means nonnegative nodes are already increasing, while negative nodes arrive from closest to zero toward most negative.
Prepend each negative node to reverse that subsequence and append each nonnegative node to a second chain, then join them.
Detach each node; negative goes to front, otherwise to nonnegative tail; connect negative tail to nonnegative head.
Reversing absolute-ordered negatives produces increasing actual values, nonnegatives retain increasing order, and every negative is no greater than every nonnegative.
